1.outline: Term theme: 'Slides + AI Game Makers'. Recap and extend slide design principles: layout, alignment, contrast and consistency.
1.sowResources: Google Slides, PowerPoint, design principles handout.
objectives: Recap and extend slide design principles.
Identify alignment and contrast problems in an example slide.
Apply the principles to a new slide.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Design critique
plan.detail: Critique a poorly designed example slide: alignment, contrast, clutter.

plan.title: Apply the fix
plan.detail: Redesign the example slide applying good layout and contrast.

plan.title: Compare
plan.detail: Compare before and after with a partner. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I identified design problems in an example slide.
I redesigned it applying good layout and contrast.
I can explain the improvement to a partner.

2.outline: Learn to add hyperlinks between slides, turning a linear deck into a choose-your-own-path presentation.
objectives: Add a hyperlink from one slide to another.
Build a simple 'choose your path' structure.
Test all the links work correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: How hyperlinks work in slides
plan.detail: Demo linking a shape or text to jump to a different slide.

plan.title: Build a branching deck
plan.detail: Build a small 'choose your path' deck with at least two branching links.

plan.title: Test the links
plan.detail: Click through every link to check it goes where expected. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I added a working hyperlink between slides.
My deck has at least two branching paths.
I tested every link works correctly.

3.outline: Create a score variable in Scratch, and add and display it so a click or key press increases the score.
objectives: Create a variable in Scratch.
Change the variable when an event happens.
Display the variable on the stage.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is a variable?
plan.detail: Recap variables as labelled boxes that hold a changing value.

plan.title: Build a score counter
plan.detail: Create a 'score' variable, increase it on a click event, and show it on the stage.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Test clicking multiple times and check the score updates. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I created a score variable.
My score increases when the event happens.
The score is visible on the stage.

4.outline: Use an if/else block to check a typed answer and respond correctly or incorrectly.
objectives: Use an if/else block to check an answer.
Give correct feedback for right and wrong answers.
Combine if/else with the score variable.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: If/else demo
plan.detail: Demo asking a question and checking the answer with if/else.

plan.title: Build a quiz question
plan.detail: Build one quiz question that checks the answer and updates the score on if correct.

plan.title: Test both paths
plan.detail: Test with a correct and an incorrect answer. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I used an if/else block to check an answer.
My quiz gives different feedback for right and wrong.
The score updates correctly when the answer is right.

5.outline: Under teacher guidance, use an AI tool to generate quiz question ideas for the game, then choose and refine the best ones.
objectives: Use a guided AI tool to generate quiz question ideas.
Choose the best generated ideas.
Refine a question so it fits the game.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Generate ideas
plan.detail: Under supervision, ask the guided AI tool for quiz question ideas on a chosen topic.

plan.title: Choose and refine
plan.detail: Pick the best 3-4 ideas and edit them to fit the quiz game.

plan.title: Discuss
plan.detail: Discuss: did the AI ideas need editing? Why? Log out.

successCriteria: I used the guided AI tool to generate question ideas.
I chose the best ideas for my game.
I edited at least one question to fit better.

6.outline: Build the full quiz game in Scratch, using the AI-generated questions, variables and if/else blocks together.
objectives: Combine variables and if/else into a multi-question quiz.
Use the AI-generated questions from last lesson.
Test the whole quiz runs correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build the quiz
plan.detail: Build 3-4 quiz questions using the score variable and if/else checking, using the refined AI questions.

plan.title: Full test
plan.detail: Play through the whole quiz and check the score is correct at the end. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My quiz has multiple questions using if/else.
My quiz uses the AI-generated questions.
My score is correct at the end of a full playthrough.

7.subtopic: Improve It After a Friend Plays
7.outline: Have a friend play the quiz game, note what confused them, and make one improvement.
objectives: Watch a friend play the quiz without helping.
Note what confused them.
Make one improvement based on the feedback.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Silent user test
plan.detail: Swap with a partner and play their quiz without help, noting any confusion.

plan.title: Improve it
plan.detail: Return to your own quiz and fix one thing the tester found confusing.

plan.title: Re-test
plan.detail: Re-test the fix works. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I tested a partner's quiz and gave honest feedback.
I made one improvement to my own quiz.
I re-tested that the improvement worked.

8.outline: Present the finished AI-assisted quiz game to the class, explaining how the score and if/else logic work.
objectives: Present the finished quiz game.
Explain how the score and if/else logic work.
Save the finished game to the portfolio.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Showcase
plan.detail: Present the game to the class or a small group, letting others play a question.

plan.title: Explain the logic
plan.detail: Explain how the score variable and if/else blocks work together.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save the finished game to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my finished quiz game.
I explained how the score and if/else work together.
My game is saved to the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Extend the quiz game with a second round of questions, reusing the score variable across both rounds.
objectives: Add a second round of questions.
Keep the score variable working across both rounds.
Test the full extended quiz.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add round two
plan.detail: Add 2-3 more questions in a second round, adding to the same score variable.

plan.title: Full test
plan.detail: Play through both rounds and check the final score is correct.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

activities: Add a second round of questions
successCriteria: My quiz now has two rounds.
The score carries correctly across both rounds.
I tested the full extended quiz.

10.outline: Rehearse the term's skills in pairs: a variable, an if/else check, and a hyperlinked or interactive element.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's skills in order.
Rehearse building a small variable-and-if/else task with a partner.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Skill recap
plan.detail: Recap: variable, if/else, AI ideas, user-test — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Build a small variable-and-if/else task with a partner reading the task card, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's skills in order.
I rehearsed the practical task with a partner.
I know which step needs more practice.

11.outline: Individual task: build a working quiz game (Scratch or interactive slides) using a score variable and if/else, tested by a peer.
objectives: Build a working quiz game with a score variable.
Use if/else to check answers correctly.
Have the game tested by a peer.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task.

plan.title: Build the game
plan.detail: Individual practical: build a small quiz with a score variable and if/else checking.

plan.title: Peer test
plan.detail: Swap with a partner for a quick test and note of any issues.

plan.title: Celebrate
plan.detail: Save and celebrate the year's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: My quiz uses a score variable correctly.
My quiz uses if/else to check answers.
A peer tested my quiz and it worked.

12.outline: Plan a bigger final quiz game with three rounds, a timer or lives system, and a proper ending screen.
objectives: Plan a three-round quiz with an extra feature (timer or lives).
Sketch the variables needed.
Plan the ending screen.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Plan the quiz
plan.detail: Sketch three rounds, the extra feature, and the variables each will need.

plan.title: Pitch it
plan.detail: Tell a partner the plan. Collect plans. Log out.

successCriteria: My plan covers three rounds and one extra feature.
My plan lists the variables I'll need.
I can tell a partner my plan.

13.outline: Build the bigger quiz game, following the plan: three rounds, the extra feature, and the score variable throughout.
objectives: Build the three quiz rounds.
Add the planned extra feature.
Test the game runs from start to finish.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build the quiz
plan.detail: Follow the plan to build three rounds and the extra feature.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Play through start to finish and fix anything broken. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My quiz has three working rounds.
My extra feature works as planned.
I tested the whole game start to finish.

14.outline: Add an ending screen showing the final score, and rehearse presenting the finished game.
objectives: Add an ending screen showing the final score.
Rehearse presenting the game.
Save the finished project.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add the ending
plan.detail: Add a screen at the end that shows the final score.

plan.title: Rehearse
plan.detail: Practise presenting the game to a partner.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save the finished project. Log out.

successCriteria: My game has an ending screen showing the score.
I rehearsed presenting it to a partner.
My finished project is saved.

15.outline: Present the finished Ultimate Quiz to the class as an arcade-style showcase, and save the year's portfolio.
objectives: Present the finished quiz confidently.
Let classmates play and see their score.
Save the whole year's portfolio.

plan.title: Final rehearsal
plan.detail: One last run-through with a partner before presenting.

plan.title: Quiz Arcade
plan.detail: Present games in small groups, letting classmates play.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save the finished game and review the whole year's portfolio folder.

plan.title: Year celebration
plan.detail: Name three things learned this year. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my quiz confidently.
Classmates played my quiz and saw their score.
My whole year's work is saved in the portfolio.
